title: Config safety harness: dry-run executor and circuit-breaker for Private/VPC/on-prem
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Implement a non-invasive 'config safety harness' for optimization recommendations in Private/VPC/on-prem deployments. The harness performs a local dry-run of batching/caching/quantization recommendations without changing runtime configs in production networks, enforces policy lint checks, and provides a circuit-breaker that prevents automatic applies when offline constraints or policy violations are detected. The feature targets teams using Redwood Private and on-prem packages that require air-gapped or restricted-network operations and strict auditability for config changes.

Goals: 
- Provide a reproducible dry-run executor that simulates the effective runtime cost/latency impact of suggested changes (batch sizes, KV cache TTLs, quantization profiles) using local metrics and sampled trace replays.
- Enforce a policy-lint stage that validates suggested config changes against org policies (e.g., forbid kernel-level changes without manual review, restrict memory-growth > 20% in on-prem hosts).
- Introduce a circuit-breaker that blocks automatic applies for suggestions that: require internet access, exceed configured resource deltas, or lack required approvals for sensitive customers.
- Default to safe, conservative suggestions for Private deployments; explicit opt-in required for aggressive changes.
- Produce detailed audit records suitable for KMS-backed signing and export to customer SIEMs.

Non-goals: 
- This ticket does not implement the full UI rollout workflow in Console. It will expose APIs/hooks for Console/CLI to call the harness.
- It does not change hosted API behavior. Hosted inference follow separate policies.

Design notes: 
1) Dry-run executor: 
   - Runs on a control-plane replica that has read-only access to local telemetry snapshots (no outbound network dependencies). 
   - Replays a sampled window of past requests (up to 10k calls per run) through the proposed config in a sandboxed simulator that mirrors KV cache semantics and batching behavior. 
   - Produces a delta report with estimated per-token cost change, p95 latency delta, memory footprint delta, and a risk score (0-100).

2) Policy-lint stage: 
   - Rules are defined as lightweight JSON/YAML policy files in the customer's config repo. Examples: max_memory_increase_pct: 20, require_manual_approval_for_quantization: true, allow_offline_runs: true. 
   - Lint step runs the policy engine locally; violations produce structured error codes and human-readable remediation hints.

3) Circuit-breaker & approvals: 
   - If the risk score > threshold or a policy violation is present, the harness emits a 'blocked' state. 
   - For Private/on-prem installs, default policy sets the breaker to BLOCK and requires at least one platform-admin manual approval. 
   - Approvals are recorded with signer identity and timestamp; records are signed with the instance's key material and persisted to the audit store.

4) Offline-first constraints: 
   - No outbound calls allowed by default in air-gapped installs; the harness must operate purely on local telemetry dumps and preloaded model artifacts. 
   - Where required, the harness supports an explicit 'allow-telemetry-sync' mode that operators can enable for controlled sync windows. 

Acceptance criteria: 
- Dry-run executor can be invoked via internal API and completes a run within an SLO (default 15 minutes for 10k sample).
- Generated delta report includes cost/latency/memory/risk fields and a machine-readable list of simulated errors.
- Policy-lint evaluates policy files and returns pass/fail with codes; built-in policy set covers at least 8 common constraints used by enterprise customers.
- Circuit-breaker prevents API endpoint that would perform an automatic apply from succeeding when in BLOCKED state. 
- Audit trail entries include signer identity, KMS key id, and rollback token; entries are exportable to S3 or local syslog.

Rollout plan: 
- Phase 1 (this ticket): core harness proof-of-concept for Private VPC images + local API. Delivery to on-prem beta customers for manual testing.
- Phase 2: integrate with Console to show dry-run results and capture approvals (follow-up ticket).
- Phase 3: Add scheduled local 'safety scans' and automatic suggested change MR generation into customer's config repo (follow-up).

Metrics to track: 
- Fraction of suggested changes that are blocked by policy-lint (target 30-60% initially).
- False-positive blocking rate (requests where harness blocks but operator approves without issues) < 10% after two iterations.
- Time-to-dry-run median under 6 minutes for 2k samples.

Risks & mitigations: 
- Risk: Simulator divergence vs real runtime. Mitigation: include a 'canary apply' sandbox mode that applies to a single dedicated host pool in Dedicated deployments (follow-up).
- Risk: Operator confusion around offline behavior. Mitigation: clear UX text, CLI flags, and a small runbook included in the audit export.

Artifacts & links: 
- Design notes draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Config+Safety+Harness
- Simulator prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/safety-harness-proto/pulls/12
- Related tickets: ENG-39108 (telemetry snapshot API), ENG-39211 (audit-store enhancements).

Next steps: 
- Spike: finish simulator accounting for KV cache eviction semantics (owner: Diego, 3d).
- Implement policy-lint engine with 6 initial rules (owner: Aisha, 5d).
- Wire KMS-signed audit entries into local audit-store (owner: Diego, 4d).
